item.title: This US Navy “Lightning Carrier” Just Sailed Up to China’s Backdoor
item.description: The USS Tripoli is not quite an aircraft carrier—but her complement of F-35s serve as a shot across the bow to China after its recent exercises around Taiwan. The post This US Navy “Lightning Carrier” Just Sailed Up to China’s Backdoor appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The US Military Once Had a Much Bigger Presence in Greenland
item.description: At its height, the United States operated 50 military installations in Greenland—and once had fantastical plans for an elaborate nuclear missile network underneath its ice. The post The US Military Once Had a Much Bigger Presence in Greenland appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: “Virtual Reality” Training Could Be a Godsend for the US Army
item.description: The Army has already begun some "virtual reality" training—using VR headsets to prepare soldiers to operate vehicles without needing them to be physically present at those vehicles’ location. The post “Virtual Reality” Training Could Be a Godsend for the US Army appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: 2025 Was a Really, Really Bad Year to Be a Russian Soldier
item.description: An estimated 415,000 Russian soldiers were killed or wounded on the battlefields of Ukraine in 2025. Astonishingly, this was not the deadliest year of the conflict. The post 2025 Was a Really, Really Bad Year to Be a Russian Soldier appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Iran’s Strategy of Delay
item.description: The Islamic Republic is gambling on US attention on its brutality eventually subsiding. The post Iran’s Strategy of Delay appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Egypt Just Sent a Warship into Israeli Waters
item.description: The ongoing Gaza War has infuriated Egypt, which sees it as a flashpoint for a regional refugee crisis. The post Why Egypt Just Sent a Warship into Israeli Waters appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Britain Is Betting Big on the “DragonFire” Anti-Drone Laser
item.description: The “DragonFire” laser system will cost as little as £10 per shot—a vast decrease from existing anti-drone missiles, which can cost tens of thousands at a minimum. The post Britain Is Betting Big on the “DragonFire” Anti-Drone Laser appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: From Paperwork to Power: Trump’s Warfighting Pentagon Takes Shape
item.description: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has empowered “Portfolio Acquisition Executives” in the Air Force to make quick contracting decisions, end-running the Pentagon’s mountains of bureaucracy. The post From Paperwork to Power: Trump’s Warfighting Pentagon Takes Shape appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: DARPA Wants to Turn the Arctic Transparent with New Radars
item.description: The “Frosty” radar system’s operation is vastly different from existing radars—and could be less disrupted by the Arctic’s harsh conditions as a result. The post DARPA Wants to Turn the Arctic Transparent with New Radars appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How China’s H-20 Stealth Bomber Could Break America’s Pacific Defense
item.description: Aircraft stealth technology is decades old, and China has demonstrated an innovative streak in its defense affairs—so Beijing’s claims about the H-20’s stealth capabilities should be taken seriously.
